picker.title: Choose a program
picker.subtitle: Your weights and history carry over either way.
picker.standardBody: Squat, bench and row on A; squat, press and deadlift on B. Five sets of five at one weight — clear every rep and the weight goes up next session.
picker.madcowBody: Ramped sets up to one top set, on a heavy–light–medium week. Squats every session, incline bench on the light day, and weight up once a week.

confirm.toMadcowBody: Your current weights become your five-rep max. A 4-week on-ramp starts you lighter and has you matching your best in week 4.
confirm.toStandardBody: Each lift keeps the top set it reached on Madcow as its working weight, and every set goes back to the same load.
confirm.endsWorkout: This ends the workout you have open.

standard.note: The same weight for all five sets. Clear all five and it goes up next session — miss any rep and it stays where it is.
standard.customiseNote: 5×5 is the program. Change it and you're running your own variation — progression stays the same.

madcow.subtitle: Sets and weights are calculated from each lift's top set. Adjust the top sets, not the ramp.
madcow.onrampNote: Deliberately light. In week 4 you match your old best, and you set records after that.
madcow.matchingNote: This week's top sets equal the weights you came in with.
madcow.recordNote: Every top set from here is a personal record.
madcow.dayANote: Five ramp sets of five. You repeat the weight you tripled last Friday — for five reps this time.
madcow.dayBNote: Squat sets one to three, then set three again. The second press and the deadlift do their own progression here.
madcow.dayCNote: Four ramp sets, then a heavier triple, then a back-off eight at your third-set weight.
howSteps: Workout C is the feeler: you lift a heavier weight for three reps.
The next Monday, workout A repeats that same weight — but for five reps.
Hit it, and Friday goes up again. Miss it, and the top set stays put.
Press and deadlift live in the light day and progress on their own each week.
madcow.secondPressNote: Madcow's light day uses the incline bench, set to about 30°. Swap it for the overhead press if you'd rather keep pressing overhead.
madcow.topSetsNote: Workout A's heaviest set of five. Every other set is worked out from it.
madcow.setIntervalNote: The gap between ramp sets. 12.5% is Madcow's default — a wider interval makes the early sets lighter.

squat: Set the bar on your upper back and unrack it.
Step back and stand with feet about shoulder-width apart.
Brace your core and keep your chest up.
Bend your hips and knees to squat down.
Lower until your hips are at or just below knee level.
Drive through your feet to stand back up.
Fully extend your hips and knees at the top.
After the final rep, walk forward and rack the bar.
bench: Lie on the bench with your eyes under the bar.
Plant your feet and grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width.
Retract your shoulder blades and unrack the bar.
Lower the bar under control to your mid-chest.
Lightly touch your chest without bouncing.
Press the bar back up until your arms are straight.
Rack the bar securely after the final rep.
row: Stand with feet hip-width apart and grip the bar just outside your legs.
Hinge at your hips until your torso is about 30–45° above horizontal.
Brace your core and keep your back flat.
Let the bar hang below your shoulders.
Pull the bar toward your lower chest or upper abdomen.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower the bar under control to full arm extension.
After the final rep, stand up and lower the bar safely.
press: Grip the bar just outside shoulder width and unrack it onto your shoulders.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and brace your core.
Move your head slightly forward as the bar passes your forehead.
Lock your elbows with the bar over your shoulders and mid-foot.
Lower the bar under control back to your shoulders.
Rack the bar after the final rep.
deadlift: Stand with the bar over the middle of your feet.
Bend at your hips and knees to grip the bar just outside your legs.
Flatten your back, brace your core, and pull the slack from the bar.
Push through your feet and stand up with the bar close to your body.
Finish standing tall without leaning backward.
Push your hips back and lower the bar past your knees.
Bend your knees and return the bar to the floor under control.
Reset your position before each repetition.
